cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. The question asks who is wise enough to explain why the land is destroyed, and then the LORD answers it Himself: “It is because they have forsaken My law…” (Jeremiah 9:13). No middleman and no guessing, friends. The One whose mouth spoke gives the reason Himself.

The answer is that they forsook His law and did not obey His voice. The LORD says they have forsaken His law, which He set before them, and they have not walked in it or obeyed His voice (Jeremiah 9:13). The reason is right there in His own words, friends. Nobody has to dig for it.
The answer is the Baals. The LORD says they followed the stubbornness of their hearts and “…gone after the Baals…” (Jeremiah 9:14). They didn't wander off by accident, bakers. They went after them.
The answer is False. The LORD says they went after the Baals “…as their fathers taught them.” (Jeremiah 9:14). It was handed down to them, friends. That's a reminder that what we pass along matters.

The answer is among nations they have never known. The LORD says He will scatter them “…among the nations that neither they nor their fathers have known…” (Jeremiah 9:16). Not just nations they hadn't met, bakers, but nations their fathers hadn't known either. That's a whole lot of unfamiliar ground.

The answer is eyes overflowing with tears. The LORD says the lament is so “…that our eyes may overflow with tears, and our eyelids may gush with water.” (Jeremiah 9:18). It's not a quiet sniffle, friends. It's a full flood. This is a sad moment, and the text lets it be sad.

The answer is True. The wailing from Zion says, “For we have abandoned the land because our dwellings have been torn down.” (Jeremiah 9:19). The homes are torn down and the people have left, friends. I think that's a hard thing to say out loud.

The answer is death. The text says, “For death has climbed in through our windows; it has entered our fortresses…” (Jeremiah 9:21). Even the fortresses weren't shut to it, bakers. This is the reason the women are told to lament.

The answer is False. The LORD says they will fall like newly cut grain behind the reaper, “…with no one to gather it.” (Jeremiah 9:22). This is one of the heavy parts of the passage, friends, and the text doesn't soften it.

The answer is riches. The LORD says, “Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the wealthy man in his riches.” (Jeremiah 9:23). Wisdom, strength and riches are the three on the list, friends. That's a whole pile of things people brag about.

The answer is that he understands and knows the LORD. The LORD says, “But let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me…” (Jeremiah 9:24). So the boast isn't about what you've got, bakers. It's about knowing Him. Now THAT is worth bragging about.

The answer is False. The LORD says He exercises loving devotion, justice and righteousness on the earth, “…for I delight in these things…” (Jeremiah 9:24). Not tolerates, friends. Delights. That tells you a lot about the One worth knowing.
The answer is True. The list in the LORD's words is “Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab…” (Jeremiah 9:26). Judah is right there with the others, friends. The text doesn't skip over its own people.

The answer is heart. The LORD says, “…the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.” (Jeremiah 9:26). The problem He names for Israel is in the heart, bakers. That's a good reminder to keep checking in there.
